sentences.text: Counsel for Applicant :- Santosh Kumar Pal,Agendra Sinha
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ajai Pratap Singh Chauhan Hon'ble Subhash Vidyarthi,J.
1. Heard Sri Santosh Kumar Pal, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Jayant Singh Tomar, learned AGA-I and perused the records.

2. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
206 of 2021, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC & 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Itaunja, District Lucknow.

3. The aforesaid case has been registered on the basis of an F.I.R. lodged on 07.08.2021 alleging that the informant's daughter aged about 14 years, who had left home for going to school on 06.08.2021 did not return home.
4. In the statement of the informant's daughter recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., she stated that she knows the applicant for the past 5-6 months and she loves him.
She had gone with the applicant out of her own free will.

A copy of the extract of voter list has been annexed with the affidavit filed in Sushil vs State Of U.P. Thru Secy. Home Lucknow on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158438633/
1 support of the bail application which contains the name of the victim and her age is mentioned to be 18 years.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. In the pathological examination report, no live or dead spermatozoa or gonococci were seen.
The statements of the informant and the victim have been recorded by the trial court and the victim has not supported the prosecution case before the trial court.

6. In the affidavit filed in support of bail application it has been stated that the applicant is innocent,
he has been falsely implicated in the present case and he has no criminal history.
7. The learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail but he could not dispute the aforesaid aspects of the matter.

8. Having considered the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the fact that the victim appears to be major, she has not supported the prosecution case before the trial court and since the statements of the informant and the victim have already been recorded, the applicant will not be in a position to influence the witnesses in case he is released on bail, coupled with the fact that the applicant has no previous criminal history and he is languishing in jail since 18.08.2021 and without making any observation, which may affect the merits of the case, I am of the view that the aforesaid facts are sufficient for making out a case for enlargement of the applicant on bail in the aforesaid crime.
9. Accordingly, this bail application stands allowed.

10. Let the applicant-Sushil be released on bail in Case Crime No. 206 of 2021, under Sections 363,
366, 376 IPC & 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Itaunja, District Lucknow on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of magistrate/court concerned.
11.

Before parting with this case, it is observed that in Hariom Sharma v. State of U.P., 2022 (120)
ACC 251, a coordinate Bench of this Court had held as under:-
"10......Neither accused nor victim or any witnesses should be permitted to subvert a criminal trial by stating falsehood and resort to contrivances, so as to make it theatre of the absurd.

entities.text:
Hariom Sharma v. State of U.P., 2022 (120)
ACC 251
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Dispensation of justice in a criminal trial is a serious issue and cannot be allowed to become a mockery by simply allowing prime prosecution witnesses /victims to turn hostile as a ground of acquittal.
Complainants should also be accountable and should take responsibility on their shoulder.
11. Considering the societal interest, it is high time for the trial court to resort to Section 344 Cr.P.C in appropriate cases.

In the present case since the prosecutrix before the trial Court has turned hostile and completely denied the prosecution version, therefore she is not entitled to the benefit of any compensation paid by the Government, which has been collected from the taxpayers of the country.

In view of the above trial Court shall consider the issuance of necessary direction against the alleged prosecutrix/ victim to refund the amount of compensation, if any received by her, in the appropriate head of the treasury account and shall also ensure the compliance of provisions of section 344 Cr.P.C at the appropriate stage, if it deems fit and proper under the facts and circumstances of the case.
13
-Office is directed to transmit a copy of this order to the court concerned within a week for compliance."
12. In the present case also the victim/ informant levelled an allegation of rape but subsequently she turned hostile and said that the alleged offence did not take place.
13. The trial court is directed to take action as per the aforesaid direction issued by this Court, in present matter also.
